name: Louis Law
life: “I still remember helping my first nervous driver to stop apologizing.” On Wednesday, near Harbour Bakery, Louis buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I teach under pressure for a living. I want my learner to get through one bend without apologizing for taking time.
appearance: Louis is easy to recognize by short black hair swept back and a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Usually dressed in an old plum windbreaker with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial, Louis starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak when listening.
personality: Louis loves an audience until a private hurt enters the room. Then the performer disappears and someone very good at getting other people through a door takes over.
agenda: To get the learner through one bend without apology.
family: Sofia Ayala is Louis’s older cousin. Louis gets to change the plan. Sofia offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The guarantee*, Sofia says, “I understand every page I signed. I would like the children to stop treating my generosity as a symptom.”
connections: Terry March. The instructor hears the difference between paid lessons and years of parental practice.

reactions.situation: Two people qualify for the same funded lesson
reactions.response: Louis asks both applicants which transport difficulty one lesson would actually address.

reactions.situation: A driver splashes a market worker and tries to laugh it off
reactions.response: Louis asks the driver to come back on foot and look at the damaged goods before discussing cost.
